summary: The note examines the economic costs of internet downtime, using a major ISP outage on September 15, 2023 in the Northeast US as a case study. It covers losses across finance, e-commerce, manufacturing, and technology, plus downstream effects on consumers and workers. It also covers historical trends, policy responses such as a proposed 99.99% uptime bill, a Conexus estimate of $55 billion in annual US losses, and preventative measures.
one_line: Case study of the September 15, 2023 ISP outage showing how internet downtime causes sector-wide economic losses and prompts policy and prevention efforts.
key_facts: On September 15, 2023 at 10:32 AM EST, a major ISP outage hit corporate offices, e-commerce platforms, and online services in the Northeast United States.
Alan Richardson, IT manager at a New York-based financial firm, said trading was suspended within minutes, costing an estimated $200,000 per hour.
E-commerce retailers raked in $5.7 trillion worldwide in 2022 according to analysts.
Startup owner Emily Harris said her online clothing store suffered a 70% reduction in daily sales due to the September outage.
Howard Chang, owner of a small restaurant chain in Boston, noted a steep drop in customer engagement for businesses using online reservation or ordering services.
The first recorded substantial internet outage occurred in 1996.
A study by Dr. Samantha Kleinberg of the University of California found the cumulative cost of internet outages has increased tenfold since 2010.
A cloud service provider CEO said service-level agreement penalties amounted to upward of $300,000 for just an hour of downtime.
An automotive plant in Detroit halted production during the September blackout, with an estimated loss of $600,000 for that day.
A study published in October 2023 by the Consumer Technology Association found consumer trust in digital services dips following major outages.
Senator John Abrams proposed a bill requiring ISPs to maintain a minimum uptime of 99.99% with substantial penalties for failing to do so.
A November 18, 2023 report by the think tank Conexus estimated the US economy could be losing up to $55 billion annually due to internet disruptions.
GlobalNet Solutions has begun to market proactive monitoring tools designed to predict outages and initiate fail-safes.
The September 2023 incident accelerated conversations about creating a national Internet resilience framework.
